title: Cross-team SLO Contracts and Capacity Mediation Guide
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This guide defines a lightweight, actionable contract pattern for cross-team SLOs and a structured mediation procedure for resolving contested capacity requests. It is intended for service owners, product engineers, platform teams, and SREs who must negotiate performance targets and capacity allocations for shared inference services.

Purpose

- Reduce friction when teams request dedicated capacity or priority routing.
- Provide a repeatable decision flow for settling SLOs, error budget allocations, and capacity gating.
- Ensure operational observability and tooling are in place before a binding SLO contract is approved.

Scope

Applies to:
- Redwood-hosted model endpoints and Dedicated GPU pools.
- Any service that consumes shared inference capacity (hosted API tenants, internal batch jobs, and integrations).
Excludes: on-prem private deployments, which follow Customer Private Deployment SLAs but should reuse this template where helpful.

Principles

1) Contracts are explicit and timeboxed: every cross-team SLO agreement is a 90-day contract by default.
2) Error budgets are the control plane: allocation decisions are based on measurable error budget impact, not anecdote.
3) Observability before commitment: no contract is accepted without tracing, latency histograms, token-cost estimates, and load tests.
4) Least privilege for capacity: prefer routing/policy changes over long-lived reserved capacity when possible.

SLO Contract Template (fillable)

- Service name: <service>
- Consumer team: <team>
- Owner: <primary owner email>
- Contract period: <start date> -> <end date> (default 90 days)
- SLO metric: p95 latency for generate endpoint (ms) / availability (%) / correctness metric (pass rate)
- Target: e.g., p95 <= 250ms, availability >= 99.5%
- Error budget: 0.5% over contract period = <allowed minutes>
- Capacity commitment: e.g., 2x c5-gpu-equivalent sustained; burst policy up to 4x for 10 minutes every 6 hours
- Cost allocation: billback model (usage-based) or internal chargeback agreed? <yes/no>
- Observability requirements: span sampling 1%, token breakdown per request, heatmap and SLI dashboard id
- Rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours with rollback on >50% of error budget burn in any 6h window
- Acceptance criteria checklist: load test results, dry-run traces, load spike simulation, security review complete

Capacity Mediation Procedure (step-by-step)

1) Request initiation: consumer files a Contract Request (CR) in the SRE intake tracker with fields from template.
2) Triage (24 hours): SRE triages request, assigns Impact score (Low/Medium/High) using the Impact Matrix below.
3) Data collection (3 business days): run load-test harness with representative prompt sets; collect p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, token cost per request.
4) Draft proposal (SRE + consumer): propose either routing policy change, caching strategy, quantization profile, or reserved capacity. Include cost estimate (USD/mo) and error budget projection.
5) Mediation meeting (if contested): 1-hour session with SRE chair, consumer PO, platform capacity owner, and an arbitration engineer. Decision recorded in CR.
6) Decision and contract signing: approved contracts are written into the SLO registry and scheduled for enforcement.
7) Review checkpoint at 30 and 75 days: verify telemetry and adjust if necessary.

Impact Matrix (summary table)

| Impact | Description | Typical outcome | Decision owner |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Low | Minor SLO change, <1% projected error budget burn | Routing tweak / cache | SRE + consumer |
| Medium | Noticeable cost or capacity shift, 1–5% error budget | Temporary reserved capacity, increased monitoring | Platform + SRE |
| High | >5% error budget or cross-service risk | Formal capacity allocation, possible cost commit | Exec-level approval (SRE Manager + Product) |

Runbook: Immediate Actions for Contract Breach (error budget burn or latency regression)

1) Automated signal fires: SLO alert -> create incident with tag slo-contract:<id>.
2) Triage: SRE oncall evaluates whether to throttle consumer or enable fallback routing.
3) Rapid mitigations (first 15 minutes):
   - Enable model-fallback policy (reduce model size or change quantization profile).
   - Increase batching or activate cached-prefix route.
   - Temporarily throttle non-critical consumer flows via edge policy.
4) Escalation (15–60 minutes):
   - If mitigations fail, convene mediation panel. Consider emergency capacity borrow from less critical tenants.
5) Post-incident: automated evidence collection and contract review meeting within 3 business days.

Tooling and Automation (minimum required integrations)

- SLO Registry: Git-backed YAML stored in /infra/slo-registry (example below). Syncs to the SLO dashboard.
- Load-test harness: infra/bench/inference-load (runbook script provided).
- Capacity simulator: runs predictive cost and error budget burn projections for proposed contract.
- Alerting: PagerDuty escalation path: slo-contract policy -> SRE oncall.
- Telemetry: Prometheus histograms, OTLP traces, per-request token metrics exported to data warehouse.

Example SLO YAML snippet (example only)

service: image-captioning-api
metric: request_latency_ms_p95
target: 250
window_days: 30
error_budget: 0.5
contact: oncall-image-captioning@sre.redwood.com
contract_id: CR-2025-045

Acceptance Checklist (pre-contract)

- [ ] Representative prompt set chosen and signed off
- [ ] Load test (50% projected traffic) completed and results attached
- [ ] Observability dashboards provisioned and shared
- [ ] Fault-injection scenario executed and rollback validated
- [ ] Cost estimate and chargeback model documented

Ownership matrix

- Consumer team: provides prompt set, business SLA, PO signoff.
- SRE: triage, load testing, drafting contract language, enforcement.
- Platform/Capacity team: capacity projection, reserved pool management, cost modeling.
- Security/Compliance: signoff for sensitive data flows.

Mediation templates and evidence to include in the CR

- Load test artifact (JTL / CSV).
- Prometheus query snapshots for p95/p99 before/after.
- Cost projection spreadsheet.
- Heatmap of per-tenant KV cache hit rates.

Governance and review cadence

- Standard contract length: 90 days (exceptions require SRE Manager approval).
- Quarterly review board: all active contracts reviewed for consolidation opportunities.
- Failed contracts: any contract with >30% error budget burn in 30 days moves to the corrective action track.

Appendix: Common Negotiation Patterns

- Prefer "priority routing + cache" over "reserved capacity" for short-lived spikes.
- If predictability trumps cost, reserve capacity but include a dynamic burst clause.
- Use canaries with progressively increasing percent and automatic rollback thresholds tied to error budget burn.

Contacts and escalation

- SRE intake board: sre-intake@redwood.com
- Emergency mediation: mediation-chair@sre.redwood.com
- Platform capacity owner: platform-capacity@redwood.com
